approach: Because no author code or bundled data exists, this is a paper-only reimplementation: acquire cs-training.csv via the Kaggle API (or manual placement after accepting rules), clean to the six listed predictors with the stated bounds, and reproduce the stratified 70/30 split. Implement ADASYN directly with k=5, adaptive majority-neighbor weights, and SMOTE-style interpolation, applied only to scaled training data; inverse-transform synthetic rows, round the three count variables, then re-scale. Train the fixed XGBoost configuration for baseline and ADASYN 1x, compute AUC/Gini on the untouched 29,173-row test set, and run a paired 1,000-iteration bootstrap for delta-AUC/p-value. The default entrypoint targets C1/C2 with a Table-1-matched N=72,817 run and also records an exact-doubling N=72,880 variant to cover the paper's textual discrepancy.

files.purpose: Install pandas, numpy, scikit-learn, xgboost, requests, tqdm; no local imports.
Central config for paths, feature list, cleaning bounds, split, ADASYN targets, XGBoost params, bootstrap settings, and output paths.
Check for data/raw/cs-training.csv and, if missing, download the Kaggle GiveMeSomeCredit competition file using KAGGLE_USERNAME/KAGGLE_KEY or ~/.kaggle/kaggle.json.

Load raw CSV, select target and six predictors, drop missing rows, apply domain bounds, audit cleaned N/default rate, create the stratified 70/30 split, and fit/apply StandardScaler on training data only.
Custom ADASYN implementation: kNN majority-neighbor ratios, normalized weights, exact synthetic budget, SMOTE interpolation, and post-generation inverse-transform/rounding of discrete count columns.
Train the fixed XGBoost classifier, compute dynamic scale_pos_weight from final training labels, and evaluate held-out test probabilities with AUC and Gini.
Compute AUC-ROC, Gini=2*AUC-1, paired 1,000-iteration bootstrap delta-AUC/delta-Gini, percentile 95% CI, and p-value as proportion of delta <= 0.
Generate a tiny in-memory or CSV synthetic dataset with the same schema for a no-Kaggle smoke test of the full data flow.
Single orchestration entrypoint: download/load data, preprocess, split/scale, run baseline and ADASYN 1x variants, optionally run ADASYN 2x/3x, run bootstrap, and write results/metrics.json.

config.missing_policy: drop rows with any missing target or predictor before capping (A1)

cleaning_bounds.DebtRatio: [0, 1.0] (A2; if cleaned N differs from 97243 by >50, audit candidates [1.0, 1.5, 2.0, 3.0, 5.0, 10.0] and record chosen cap)

config.outlier_policy: drop rows outside inclusive bounds; do not clip kept rows (A1/A2)
config.scaler: StandardScaler fit on training set only; transform train and test (R7)

adasyn.run_on: scaled training features only; test set never augmented (R8/A6)
adasyn.postprocess: inverse_transform synthetic rows, round discrete predictors to nearest integer, clip to cleaning bounds, transform back with training scaler (R5/A6)

xgboost.scale_pos_weight: n_majority/n_minority computed from final training labels after augmentation (R12/A8)

metrics.bootstrap_unit: test-set rows with replacement; same resample for baseline and ADASYN (A9)
metrics.p_value: proportion of bootstrap delta-AUC <= 0; no +1 correction (A9)

steps: Install dependencies with `python -m pip install -r requirements.txt` (pandas, numpy, scikit-learn, xgboost, requests, tqdm).

Acquire the real dataset by running `python data/download_gmsc.py`; if data/raw/cs-training.csv is absent, use KAGGLE_USERNAME/KAGGLE_KEY or ~/.kaggle/kaggle.json to download the GiveMeSomeCredit cs-training.csv. If Kaggle returns 403, stop and report that the competition rules must be accepted and the file placed manually at data/raw/cs-training.csv.

Run `python data/preprocess.py --audit` to load cs-training.csv, select SeriousDlqin2yrs plus exactly the six predictors, drop rows with any missing value, apply the configured bounds, and print raw N, cleaned N, default rate, and missing counts.

Verify the cleaned dataset is N=97,243 with default rate ~7.07%; if N differs by more than 50, run the DebtRatio cap audit over the configured candidates and record the chosen cap in results/metrics.json before proceeding.
Create the stratified split with sklearn train_test_split(test_size=0.30, stratify=y, random_state=42); assert or print train n=68,070 (4,810 defaults) and test n=29,173 (2,061 defaults).
Fit StandardScaler on X_train only, transform X_train and X_test, and verify training means are ~0 and standard deviations ~1; keep the scaler for inverse-transform/re-transform of synthetic rows.

Train the baseline XGBoost with max_depth=6, learning_rate=0.1, n_estimators=100, objective='binary:logistic', eval_metric='auc', random_state=42, and scale_pos_weight=63260/4810; predict test probabilities and compute baseline AUC/Gini.

Run ADASYN 1x Table-1-matched on scaled X_train to target minority count 9,557 (add 4,747 synthetics); inverse-transform synthetic rows, round the three discrete predictors, clip to bounds, re-transform with the training scaler, then train XGBoost with scale_pos_weight computed from the final augmented labels and evaluate test AUC/Gini.

Run the exact-doubling ADASYN 1x variant to target minority count 9,620 (add 4,810 synthetics, N_train=72,880) and record its metrics separately as the paper-text variant and its deviation from Table 1's N=72,817.

Run the paired 1,000-iteration bootstrap on the test set using the same resampled indices for baseline and Table-1-matched ADASYN 1x; compute delta-AUC, delta-Gini, percentile 95% CIs, and p-value = mean(delta-AUC <= 0).

Optionally run `python reproduce.py --all-scenarios` to train ADASYN 2x and 3x using Table 1 target minority counts 13,995 and 18,745 for C3/C4 checks; this is not required for the C1 headline reproduction.

Write results/metrics.json with data audit, split counts, baseline metrics, ADASYN 1x Table-1 metrics, exact-doubling metrics, delta-AUC/delta-Gini, bootstrap CI/p-value, and within_tolerance flags against the 0.01 absolute band for C1/C2.
smoke_test: Run `python reproduce.py --smoke`. This bypasses Kaggle, creates a tiny 400-row synthetic CSV with the same columns and ~7% positives, runs cleaning, a 70/30 stratified split, ADASYN to a small target minority count, XGBoost with n_estimators=5, and 10 bootstrap iterations, then writes results/smoke_metrics.json and asserts finite AUC/Gini and the expected JSON keys.
intermediate_checks: Raw data check: cs-training.csv loads with 150,000 rows and the expected columns including SeriousDlqin2yrs; MonthlyIncome and NumberOfDependents missing counts are printed.

Cleaned data check: after missing-row removal and bounds, N is close to 97,243, there are exactly six predictors, and the default rate is close to 7.07%; if not, report the DebtRatio cap audit before any training.
Split check: train has 68,070 rows and 4,810 positives; test has 29,173 rows and 2,061 positives. Do not touch the test set for augmentation.
Scaling check: StandardScaler is fit only on X_train; transformed training features have mean ~0 and std ~1; test is transformed with the same scaler.
ADASYN check: synthetic count equals target_minority - 4,810; no NaNs; discrete predictors are integer-valued after rounding; augmented training labels contain exactly the target minority count.

Model check: feature count is six; baseline scale_pos_weight is ~13.15; ADASYN 1x scale_pos_weight is ~6.62 for N=72,817 and ~6.58 for exact doubling; XGBoost trains without warnings that invalidate the run.

Sanity baseline: baseline test AUC should be roughly in the 0.65-0.70 range and ADASYN 1x should be near the paper's 0.6778; if far outside, inspect cleaning bounds, missing-row policy, and class-weight computation before accepting results.
Metrics check: Gini equals 2*AUC-1; bootstrap CI is ordered; p-value is in [0,1]; results/metrics.json contains both C1 and C2 fields plus the exact-doubling deviation record.
budget_plan: Setup and dependency install: 3-5 min. Data download/audit plus smoke test: 2-4 min. Full C1/C2 run (preprocess, baseline XGBoost, ADASYN 1x Table-1, exact-doubling variant, and 1,000 paired bootstrap iterations): 10-15 min. Optional 2x/3x scenarios add 5-10 min. Total should remain within roughly 20-30 min on CPU.
